rubric_items.reason: REQ-1 to REQ-16 cover all nine acceptance criteria, REQ-17 closes the gap in the tie-break, and the booking page is out of scope with a reason. REQ-2 still leaves out the ticket's condition that the window uses the same days as HMS-9 (attempt-1 F-2 is still open).

Most REQs are atomic and checkable. REQ-12 and REQ-13 give only the status and message, not the error body from conventions#errors. REQ-1 and REQ-3 also carry glossary definitions inside the behaviour statement.
Every REQ cites the ticket or an IDE answer. The old collation default is now REQ-17, confirmed by this run's A-01, so attempt-1 F-1 is resolved. Nothing invented is marked known.

Nothing clashes with the intent baseline. The no-paging exception to conventions#lists is surfaced (C8) and settled by the ticket and A-02. The scope difference with cancelled-run A-06 is disclosed only as prose, not as a recorded mismatch.
One precise, non-blocking IDE question (A-01), with real options and the right person answering. No questions are left open. Reused answers avoid asking again.
Plain and readable, and the missing glossary terms are disclosed. The id A-01 now means two different answers (this run and the cancelled run), so the reader has to rely on the qualifiers.
